newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N rates rise in new reserve period.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N rates rise in new reserve period.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interbank rates rose on the first day of the new reserve period as the banks filled up reserves, traders said on Tuesday.

"There is a new reserve period, with new reserve bases and everybody is looking at safety," said Sandor Tolonics of Budapest Bank. "This position makes the market narrower in the first few days (of the period)," he added.

The overnight rates were traded at 23 percent for most of the session and closed at 22.75 percent, compared with the 20 percent finish of Monday, when banks with full reserves laid out excess money pushing down rates.

Traders added they did not see speculation, or tax-payments disturbing the market, and the overnight rates were likely to remain around 22.75 percent, the level of the central bank's one-week reverse repo rate, this week.
